newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania's Socialists set to form new government.
newsitem.headline: Albania's Socialists set to form new government.

text.p: Albania's ex-communist Socialists prepared on Monday to form a new government after sweeping to a landslide victory in elections called to end months of mayhem and bloodshed in Europe's poorest country.

With final official results still to come after Sunday's runoff vote in 34 districts, the Socialists appeared headed for a two-thirds majority in parliament over the right-wing Democratic Party of President Sali Berisha, enabling them to push through radical legislation.

Berisha and the Democrats who ruled until March were widely blamed for tolerating shady pyramid savings schemes that collapsed earlier this year, swallowing the life savings of thousands of families and triggering upheaval.

The elections passed off relatively smoothly in a country that has been under gun rule for months, although ATA news agency reported two people were killed and two injured on Sunday when a man opened fire in a polling station in the Shkoder area in northern Albania.

A spokesman for the Central Election Commission told Reuters he had heard reports of several other violent incidents during Sunday's runoff in districts where no candidate won a majority in the first round, but had no further details.

The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), which deployed monitors for both rounds of voting, said on Sunday it knew of no irregularities serious enough to jeopardise the poll, despite complaints of intimidation by both major parties.

The first major political casualty of the elections was Democratic Party chairman Tritan Shehu, who announced on Monday he was stepping down after polling less than 30 percent in Sunday's runoff in Kavaje, near Tirana.

This appeared to open the way for Berisha to take over as party leader when he resigns or is voted out as president by the new parliament. He has already pledged to step down once a new government is in power.
His spokesman said it was too early to say who would take over the party leadership.
Socialist leader Fatos Nano confirmed on Sunday he would head a new coalition government, together with the Social Democrats and Democratic Alliance, and expected it to have a two-thirds majority.
"It is very sure now, with this already large mandate, that people voted in this election for a new way of rebuilding a democratic civilisation in Albania," he said on Sunday.
Nano has stressed during a hard-fought campaign that his reformed party had nothing in common with its predecessor, the Stalinist regime headed by isolationist Enver Hoxha that ruled for 45 years.
By concentrating on the premiership, Nano has confirmed he wants to reduce the powers of the presidency, which were increased dramatically under Berisha.

As the new government prepared to take over, Albania's self-proclaimed king Leka I vowed to continue his fight for the restoration of the monarchy despite rejection of the idea in a referendum last Sunday.
In the absence of final official referendum results, Leka challenged preliminary figures showing 66 percent had voted against the monarchy, saying the poll had been rigged.
"I don't believe the vote has gone against it," Leka told Reuters in an interview on Monday. "I can't give up, I have the trust of so many people."
